To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the State's sentinel program is not representative of Flint housing stock and (ii) there is a need to collect additional water samples from the most affected households to determine the true extent of the problem.

(1) there is no evidence that voluntary sampling was more biased than State-controlled sampling; (2) State-controlled sampling was not representative of Flint housing stock and, in particular, did not include any LSL site in the two most impoverished wards of the city; (3) correcting for sampling bias did not change the overall temporal trend of WLL, but narrowed the gap between the two sampling programs.
